transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-21
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Lee (Redwood SE), Maria (Acme Head of MLOps), Ethan (Platform Eng), Sofia (Security), Tom (Product)
Link: https://redwood.app/s/meetings/ff-20260821-ACME-0472

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on scope and immediate tasks for onboarding Acme Health onto Redwood Dedicated/Private. Focus on security requirements, benchmarking plan, and go/no-go criteria for pilot.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roundtable — I'll run through agenda, samir will cover onboarding ops, lee will talk tech/bench, and then open for questions. Maria over to you for quick intro to your goals?
[00:28] Maria: Hi, yeah thanks. So our primary objective is to replace a bunch of internal GPT endpoints with a more cost predictable infra and meet our compliance needs. We're looking at a 3-month pilot to validate performance and cost at production-like load. Key constraints: PHI-ish data, so strict egress and KMS control.
[01:10] Ethan: And infra wise we run across multi-cloud, mostly GCP with some AWS dev clusters. We'll need a VPC peering or private link into Redwood Private, and we need service accounts set up ahead of time.
[01:40] Lee: Great, that's helpful. A quick note — for benching we typically ask for representative sequences and token distributions, plus typical concurrency. That lets us recommend quantization profiles and batching.
[02:05] Samir: I'll own the project plan and gating checklist. We'll propose a timeline today and get alignment on the pilot's acceptance criteria.

[03:02] Jordan: Agenda quick: 1) timeline/milestones, 2) security/network requirements, 3) bench plan & success criteria, 4) admin/access, 5) next steps.

[04:00] Lee: On the runtime side, for Dedicated we can provision a reserved GPU pool; for high throughput we recommend splitting read-heavy embedding traffic to hosted endpoints to save cost but run generative workloads on Dedicated. There's always that latency vs cost tradeoff.
[04:42] Maria: Our product needs sub-300ms median token latency on short prompts. Is that feasible on Dedicated?
[05:00] Lee: For short prompts on a 80B quantized model on A100-equivalent nodes we typically see median token latencies in the 150-350ms range depending on KV cache hits and batching. If you need strict 100-150ms we'd discuss lower-latency model variants or smaller context lengths. Also caching prefixes helps.

[06:10] Ethan: For networking, we use Shared VPCs and Cloud NAT in GCP; how does Redwood handle private endpoints? We prefer VPC peering over public egress.
[06:36] Samir: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and PrivateLink patterns; we can describe the setup. There's usually a network firewall rule and a service account with minimum scopes. We'll send an example terraform snippet.
[07:04] Sofia: On the security side, we require KMS integration and key custody — can we bring our own keys (BYOK)? Also SOC 2, SSO and audit logs are must-haves.
[07:32] Jordan: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated; we have integrations with GCP KMS and AWS KMS, and HSM options for on-prem. We also emit audit logs and support SAML/SCIM provisioning. I'll attach the security whitepaper after the call.

[08:20] Maria: For data retention, we need a guarantee that no customer data is used for model training and a retention policy of logs for 365 days with ability to purge.
[08:45] Samir: Redwood has a 0-data-training policy by default for customer data on private deployments and Dedicated; logs retention is configurable and we can set 365 days. Purge APIs are available — I'll include links.

[09:30] Lee: Bench methodology — we'll need a staging dataset, a small traffic generator that simulates your concurrency and token lengths, and a target SLA. For the pilot we usually run a 72-hour soak with peak concurrency windows.
[10:05] Ethan: Can Redwood run the bench from your side, or do we run it from our infra?
[10:18] Lee: We can run bench agents from both sides; easiest is for you to grant a staging service account and we'll run server-side loads to replicate the network path. If you want to run it internally we provide scripts and a results workbook.

[11:05] Tom: On success criteria — we'd love to validate cost per 1M tokens under X and 99th percentile latency under Y. We'll put exact numbers in a follow-up.
[11:30] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll draft a templated success criteria doc — cost and latency plus functional correctness on a set of golden prompts.

[12:10] Maria: A couple of things — compliance team will want SOC2 report and pen test results, any red team findings. Also need to see RBAC controls and granular audit logs by token.
[12:40] Samir: We'll share SOC2 and our penetration test summary. For RBAC we support org/team roles and fine-grained permissions in the console, and audit trails tie back to request IDs.

[14:00] Lee: A technical note: depending on model size and quantization we might recommend int4/int8 quantization and kernel-selection to reduce memory footprint. That affects output fidelity; we'll measure quality regressions vs latency/cost in the bench.
[14:45] Maria: We run a lot of clinical summarization prompts, so model output quality is critical. If quantization reduces quality we'll need to consider hybrid approach.
[15:05] Lee: Absolutely, that's part of the bench: we run evals on a labeled set and surface BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics and human spot checks.

[16:00] Ethan: Integration hooks — we want streaming and function-calling for structured outputs. Are those available in Dedicated?
[16:20] Jordan: Yes, streaming and function calling are supported across deployment modes, though certain advanced runtimes have slightly different latencies. We'll document recommended routes.

[17:10] Sofia: On legal side, we'll need a data processing addendum and clear delineation of subprocessors. Who are the typical subprocessors for Dedicated?
[17:30] Samir: For Dedicated and Private, subprocessors are minimal — cloud infra vendors if you choose cloud-hosted Dedicated. For Private on-prem there are none. We'll share an up-to-date list.

[18:20] Maria: Timeline suggestion — Week 0: legal/security signoffs & staging access; Week 1: env setup & smoke tests; Week 2-3: benching and tuning; Week 4: decision meeting. Does that align?
[18:40] Jordan: That's reasonable for a three to four week ramp before a 3-month pilot. We'll align resources.

[20:00] Lee: I'll need representative sequences: typical prompt lengths, average response tokens, and peak concurrency numbers. Also any PII/PHI masking requirements so we can avoid full-text retention where needed.
[20:30] Maria: We'll provide a sanitized sample dataset and a doc with masking rules.

[22:00] Tom: Pricing — can you give a rough estimate for a reserved pool for our expected 200 qps?
[22:18] Jordan: I'll produce a pilot price estimate; rough ballpark today is dependent on model family and reserved GPU count. I'll send a formal estimate within 48 hours.

[24:00] (brief cross-talk)
[25:00] Lee: For benchmarks we'll track token/sec, median token latency, p99 latency, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also run quality evals on the labeled prompts.

[27:30] Sofia: One more security note — we want key rotation every 90 days and a clear incident response playbook.
[27:48] Samir: Noted. We'll include key rotation options and the incident response runbook.

[30:00] Jordan: OK quick recap and action owners: Samir share onboarding playbook and security docs; Lee draft bench plan; Jordan price estimate; Customer provide staging data and KMS details. Anything missing?
[30:22] Maria: That's it from us. Appreciate the clarity.

[31:00] Jordan: We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep dive and include a pre-read. Expect docs in the next 48 hours.
[31:18] Maria: Great, thanks everyone.

[31:45] (wrap up)

Recap (auto): Immediate deliverables: security pack + SOC2, onboarding playbook, staging access, bench plan and price estimate. Next meeting: SE deep dive / bench kickoff.

References mentioned: onboarding playbook (link sent after call), security whitepaper and SOC2 (will be shared), bench scripts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-scripts (note: placeholder), sample results workbook (will attach).

Action item recap (voice): 
- Lee to deliver bench plan and perf config by 2026-08-28
- Samir to share onboarding playbook + security docs by 2026-08-24
- Jordan to send pilot pricing by 2026-08-26
- Maria to provide sanitized datasets and KMS details by 2026-08-25

End of transcript
